results.resolution: No ops. The 1986 one-pitch 5.6 Southeast Face still has only one independent source, so the row cannot be re-pointed to it. Three independent accounts now describe the easy route as one line: from the south base, a slabby ledge leads around onto the east side, then a scramble on blocks reaches the summit. That is the line the sibling wa_witches_tower_south_face already holds, so this row's East Face ledge content most likely duplicates it. Owner's call: merge or delete this row (A), or re-point it to the Southeast Face on the guidebook alone (B).
results.summary: There is still no second source for the 1986 Southeast Face 5.6. Three independent accounts (2005, 2006, 2014) place the easy ledge scramble from the south base onto the east side, which is the sibling standard route, so this row's 'East Face ledges' content most likely duplicates that sibling.
results.evidence: Eighth pass, 2026-10-01. (1) Mountain Project, re-read: the Witches Tower area lists exactly ONE route, 'East Face' (4th, 1 pitch, Ice 2/M1b, 300 ft, posted 2016). Its text: 'ascends a series of zig-zagging ledges generally on the E/SE side of the tower. Many variations are possible. One included a short and solid 4th class perfect hand crack.' Approach: 'From Asgard pass, hike S/SE up moderate snow slopes ... to below the E side'. Descent: 'Reverse the route'. Protection: 'Sturdy boots'. It has no comments and no Southeast Face page. (2) NEW, a second independent account of the easy line: Washington Scrambles (Goldman, 2014), read through Google Books in-book search snippets. It goes 'south of a steep snowfield and go to the south base of Witches Tower, where you will find a ledge that you can use to get to boulders. Scramble on rock to the top of Witches Tower (8520 feet).' (3) NEW, a first-hand photo caption from 2005 on the summitpost image 'South face of Witches Tower': 'The scramble route stays to the right of the higher snow patch and traverses on a semi-exposed slabby ledge around to the east side (June 19, 2005).' The same site's peak page gives the South Route (Class 3) as: south base, 'go up towards the white wall and find a ledge to traverse around to the east side ... scrambling large black blocks', and then names 'Southeast Face goes up the white rock one pitch 5.6' as a separate line, with wording taken from Beckey. (4) The 2006 yellowleaf report (already read in r15) also describes a slabby ledge on the SSE side, then a short scramble with a bit of 3rd class. So three authors in three years describe one easy route: a ledge from the south base onto the east side, then blocks to the summit. That is the sibling wa_witches_tower_south_face ('South Face / Standard Route', Class 3, whose beta already reads 'find a ledge to traverse around the east side of the tower, then scramble large black granite blocks'). The only description of it as 4th class 'zig-zag ledges on the E/SE side' is Mountain Project, and its approach, gear (boots) and descent (reverse) all fit the scramble, not a roped climb. Nothing proves it is a different line. (5) Southeast Face 5.6, searched again on new angles, still only Beckey (Cascade Alpine Guide 2000 p.276: 'Curt Snyder and Kevin Kurtz on July 3, 1986; one pitch (5.6) climbs a chimney under loose blocks and on to the upper slabs'). Google Books legacy feed: 'Witches Tower' with Snyder, Kurtz, 'southeast face' or 5.6 returns only Beckey (2000, two listings) and Selected Climbs vol 1, which has no in-book hit for the tower. Classic Cascade Climbs (2021) names Witches Tower only on an overview map of Colchuck and Aasgard. Internet Archive full-text search ('Witches Tower' with 'southeast face', Enchantment, Aasgard; 'Witch Tower' Aasgard) again resolves only to Beckey (1973/1987/2000) and Selected Climbs. The Skookum Traveler blog (2013) is a roped West Buttress ascent (class 4 with a short class 5 chimney) plus a class-3 south-face scramble. WTA trip reports (2006, 2021, 2024) have no route on the tower. The Wikipedia article gives no routes beyond 'YDS 3 scrambling', citing Beckey. Blocked, not bypassed: peakbagger ascent list and listsofjohn (Cloudflare challenge). theCrag was not tried, being Cloudflare-blocked in r15. Why no ops: rule 3 points to the one documented climb no sibling holds, the 1986 Southeast Face, but it has one source. Stripping the row to its East Face ledge content would recreate the sibling standard route. Deleting or merging is the owner's to run; no delete ops are written. Note for the owner: the row's beta, pitch_detail, approach_variants and summit-pin directions carry the scramble ('zig-zag ledges', 4th, boots), while descent_text, itinerary and rope_note carry the 5.6 roped pitch. So the row is internally mixed whichever option is chosen.
